title: High-Throughput Beta-glucuronidase (GUS) Assay for Phaeodactylum tricornutum
author: Erin Garza
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbexijfn
materials: To lyse the cells, add 150 µl bacterial protein extraction reagent (B-PER, ThermoFisher) to each well and mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Centrifuge cultures and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer 250 μl of each Phaeodactylum tricornutum culture into a 96‑well plate, centrifuge at 3000 × g for 10 min, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Collect supernatants to new plate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate again for 10 min at 3000 × g, then carefully transfer the supernatants to a new 96‑well plate without disturbing the cell debris.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer and substrate
steps.instruction: Transfer 50 µl of each lysate to a fresh plate, add 125 µl of GUS extraction buffer containing 1 mM MUG, and incubate for 1 h at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Prepare GUS extraction buffer: 50 mM NaPO₄ H₂ (pH 7), 0.1 % Triton X‑100, and 10 µM β‑mercaptoethanol.
Add 125 µl of this buffer plus 1 mM MUG to each well containing 50 µl lysate.
Incubate the plate for 1 hour at 37 °C.

steps.title: Stop the enzymatic reaction
steps.instruction: Add 150 µl of GUS stop buffer (0.2 M Na₂CO₃) to each well and mix thoroughly by pipetting.

steps.title: Transfer quenched reaction
steps.instruction: Transfer 200 µl of the quenched reaction from each well to an opaque 96‑well plate.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Read fluorescence on a plate reader using excitation 360 nm and emission 440 nm.

steps.title: Dilute if fluorescence too high
steps.instruction: If fluorescence readings exceed the detector range, dilute the sample with additional stop buffer before re‑reading.

steps.title: Normalize to total protein
steps.instruction: Use the remaining cell lysates to perform a BCA assay (or an equivalent protein assay) to normalize GUS activity to total cell protein for each culture.
